title: Token-level latency diagnostics shim for VPC/on-prem collectors
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Introduce a lightweight diagnostics shim for VPC and on-prem collectors that captures per-request token emission timings from inference services and correlates them with collector-side backpressure and resource signals. The shim should enable fast triage of tail-token latency spikes for dedicated and private deployments without leaking tenant data or adding significant CPU/network overhead to collector paths.
technical_design: Design overview: 1) Instrumentation contract: inference runtimes emit an optional, compact token-timing header (base64-encoded delta timestamps per token) or a token-timing span in the trace envelope when enabled. 2) Collector shim: a small module inside the VPC/on-prem collector parses the token timing artifact, attaches collector metrics (queue length, active-batches, cpu_millis, egress_bytes) and produces a tied diagnostic event. 3) Sampling and privacy: token-level capture is gated by a tenant-configurable sample rate (0.01% - 10%) and always hashed/opaque tenant id. 4) Transport: diagnostics are written to a separate low-volume, high-cardinality diagnostics Kafka topic (namespaced per-customer) with a short retention (7 days) and optional customer-controlled TTL. 5) Dashboards: Kibana/Grafana heatmap and trace join views keyed by deterministic request fingerprint to correlate token emission stalls with collector backpressure and kernel-level stalls. Implementation notes: - Keep the token timing encoding compact: delta-encoded 16-bit ints with zigzag to handle negatives. - Avoid parsing full payloads; shim only extracts header or envelope field. - Expose an operator flag to disable diagnostic forwarding in air-gapped installs. - Ensure data plane path is non-blocking: enqueue diagnostic events to background writer with bounded queue; drop diagnostics when queue exceeds threshold and emit a sampling-drop metric. - Backwards compatibility: shim must treat absent token timing as a no-op.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Performance vs signal: higher sample rates give better coverage but increase collector CPU and storage. To mitigate, we rely on delta-encoding and dedicated short-retention topic and strict queueing to avoid consumer read amplification. Privacy vs usefulness: token timings could correlate with content; we mitigate by never including raw tokens, only timing deltas and hashed tenant/context ids. Operational complexity: adding a new Kafka topic and dashboarding increases operator overhead; we provide templates and a default managed retention policy for hosted Dedicated customers.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (lab): implement shim and instrumentation in a dev-only branch; enable at 0.1% sample for internal tenants. Phase 2 (canary): deploy to 3 customer VPCs with opt-in flag and run for 2 weeks; validate overhead <1% CPU and network <1MB/day per 10k requests. Phase 3 (general availability): add UI toggle in Console and expose sample-rate on per-tenant config. Phase 4 (optimize): introduce adaptive sampling tied to tail-latency alerts to increase sample rate automatically for impacted tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Shim extracts token-timing artifacts and attaches collector metrics to diagnostic events for >= 95% of instrumented requests.
End-to-end latency overhead on collector path < 1% P95 when shim enabled at 1% sample rate.
Dashboards (heatmap + trace-join) show token-level tail spikes correlated with collector queue depth in canary customers.
No raw tokens or PII are transmitted; security review signoff obtained.
Operator docs and Console toggle documented; opt-out and disable flag verified in air-gapped installs.
